proof:
# A uniform strictification of finite-base support compatibility

Let P be a finite set of distinct Euclidean base points. Let positive convex
fibers K_z satisfy all anchored Minkowski inclusions

    sum_w p_w K_w subset K_z,
    p_w>=0, sum_w p_w=1, sum_w p_w w=z.

Nontrivial representations can be taken with p_z=0: if 0<p_z<1, subtract
that term from the support inequality and divide by1-p_z. The case p_z=1
is the identity constraint.

Choose R>max_(z in P)|z|^2 and put t_z=R-|z|^2>0. With the Euclidean unit
ball B_d define K_z(epsilon)=K_z+epsilon t_z B_d. This is an actual compatible
family for every epsilon>=0. More precisely, for every unit continuous
normal u and every nontrivial anchored representation excluding z,

    h_(K_z(epsilon))(u)-sum_w p_w h_(K_w(epsilon))(u)
      =h_(K_z)(u)-sum_w p_w h_(K_w)(u)
         +epsilon sum_w p_w |w-z|^2.

If P has at least two points, the last coefficient is at least

    min{|w-z|^2:w,z in P,w!=z}>0.

Thus all such containment constraints become strict with one uniform
linear margin, independently of their normals. The calculation uses only
sum p_w w=z and sum p_w=1.

For a finite cap family, common continuous-coordinate homothety of the
body and matching homothety of the cap planes multiplies every fiber
volume and every cap volume by the same d-th power factor. It preserves
all anchored compatibility inclusions and the entire-fiber cap cover
constraints. A shrink therefore strictly decreases every positive cap
budget. Adding a sufficiently small positive multiple of the displayed
ball addition retains these strict decreases and strictly improves all
nontrivial compatibility constraints. The ball-addition volume changes
are finite to first order; the change of a fixed cap is bounded by the
total added volume in its fibers.

This provides a concrete unrestricted feasibility direction for separation
arguments whose other cap-coordinate requirements are explicitly checked.
It does not authorize the same direction in a fixed facet-count class,
does not by itself prove a second-order multiplier theorem, and does not
make arbitrary localized shape changes compatible.
